ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side of the figure is the AC input terminal. The upper branch first passes through a resistor marked 5Ω, then passes through a capacitive impedance marked -jX_C; this series part corresponds to voltage phasor U1. Its right end is connected to a parallel load: one branch is a 10Ω resistor, and the other branch is a j10Ω inductive impedance; the two ends of the parallel load correspond to voltage phasor U2. Reasoning: Denote the preceding series part as Z1 = 5 - jX_C, and denote the right-side parallel load as Z2 = 10Ω || j10Ω. Calculate Z2 = (10·j10)/(10 + j10) = 5 + j5, therefore the phase angle of Z2 is 45°. Since Z1 and Z2 are in series in the overall circuit, the current flowing through them is the same, so the phase difference between U1 and U2 is equal to the impedance phase angle difference between Z1 and Z2. The problem requires U1 to lag U2 by 90°, that is, angle(Z1) - angle(Z2) = -90°. Therefore angle(Z1) = -45°. And Z1 = 5 - jX_C, whose phase angle satisfies tan(angle Z1) = -X_C/5. Let angle(Z1) = -45°, obtaining X_C/5 = 1, so X_C = 5Ω.

method.method_draft: Model the image circuit with Z1 = 5 - jX_C and Z2 = 10 || j10 = 5 + j5. Form the phasor ratio U1/U2 = Z1/Z2 = (5 - jX_C)/(5 + j5).
